newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Gasoline steady, two deals done.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Gasoline steady, two deals done.

text.p: Singapore gasoline were steady with two deals seen traded late Thursday while naphtha firmed despite a huge build in light distillates stocks.
A 92-octane gasoline was sold by a Dutch trader at $22.65 per barrel for August 11-15 loading while a 97-octane cargo for August 12-16 loading was traded at $24.15 per barrel.
Traders said prices had held steady with the fresh buying interest but regional supplies remained adequate to meet demand.
Thailand is quiet with no signs of any export or import tenders, traders said.
India has issued a tender to buy 25,000/T 87.15 octane leaded gasoline for delivery to August 10-14. The tender closes July 24 and is valid for one day.
Traders said the tender will helped boost current soft sentiment.
A major said he has some gasoline barrels to sell in August but is not in a hurry to sell and would rather place them in storage.
The trade development board weekly stocks figures showed that there have been a marginal increase in imports of regular gasoline but a relatively bigger drop in exports.
On premium grade, there was a drop in imports and an increase in exports of about the same volume.
The gains seen on light distillates stocks were mostly on naphtha which showed a dropped in exports and a build in imports.
But naphtha levels firmed despite the build in stocks. Traders attributed the strong market to a firm European market.
The naphtha swaps rose about five cents from Wednesday with August last quoted at $21.75/$21.90 per barrel.
Regional demand is strong due to the high operating rates of ethylene and aromatics plant, traders said.
India has tendered to sell 28,000 tonnes of HAN for August 3-5 loading from Bombay and another tender to sell 25,000 tonens of NGL loading July 31 to August 2 from Hazira.
Both tenders will close July 24 and is valid for one day.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
